title: Untangling Input Language from Reasoning Language: A Diagnostic Framework for Cross-Lingual Moral Alignment in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: A 2x2 factorial framework that independently manipulates the input language and reasoning language (English vs. Chinese) of moral dilemmas to measure verdict flip rates and isolate whether inconsistencies stem from language comprehension or language generation.

Applying Moral Foundations Theory to calculate 'moral fingerprints' via regression analysis, measuring how an LLM's prioritization of moral dimensions (e.g., Equality, Loyalty, Authority) shifts across Western-leaning (AITA) and Chinese-origin (CMoral) cultural contexts.
